business_problem: Swisscom needed to help banking users search and summarize a fast-growing library of more than 3,500 industry documents with better speed, relevance, and trust than general-purpose online AI tools could provide.
solution_summary: Swisscom built a retrieval-augmented generation service for e.foresight, its banking-industry think tank, by putting the entire document library on MongoDB Atlas and using MongoDB Vector Search to ground LLM responses. Reports, live-event recordings, graphics, and external studies are stored in Atlas as the single secure repository, then vectorized so the application can retrieve relevant segments and feed domain-specific context into large language models. The team went from first contact with MongoDB on February 6 to a working subset prototype by February 15, then production in early May after joint testing with ZHAW and internal operations handoff. Because the data stays in Switzerland and every answer can point back to cited source material, Swisscom can serve banks with faster, more accurate summaries while meeting the trust and sensitivity requirements of the financial sector.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores e.foresight's banking research corpus and operational data in one secure repository.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Vector Search
solution_components.role: Retrieves the most relevant document segments to ground AI-generated responses for banking users.

data_flow: Reports, event recordings, graphics, and external studies are stored in MongoDB Atlas, converted into embeddings, searched with MongoDB Vector Search, and the retrieved context is passed to LLMs so e.foresight users receive condensed, source-linked answers instead of manual document lists.
business_outcome: Swisscom stood up the first solution with about six days of development effort, moved from concept to prototype in days, improved the speed and relevance of banking-content searches and summaries, and created a reusable pattern for additional Swiss AI Platform services.
